Open-book reference: EDC Weeks 1–10 (full course)

Covers every week, 1 to 10, and replaces the short Weeks 1–5 strip of the earlier version. Boylestad notation throughout ( model, hybrid-π, , , ). Work in mA, kΩ, mS and V: then mA × kΩ = V and mS × kΩ is a plain gain. is the thermal voltage, 25.875 mV ≈ 26 mV at 27 °C. BJT small-signal work uses (WS6 Q1–Q3 use 25 mV: follow the question). For FETs, is the E-MOSFET threshold (written in the Sedra questions; it is not the thermal voltage). or not given means : say so in your answer. Course constants: V, V, Si knee 0.7 V. All check values below were recomputed in Python.

pn junction (qualitative, MCQs). Open circuit: majority carriers diffuse and recombine, leaving immobile ionised dopants (+ on n side, − on p side) = depletion region; its field sets the barrier and drives the minority drift current ; at equilibrium (no net current). Charge balance , so : the region extends into the lightly doped side; –1 µm. . Forward bias: barrier lowered, shrinks, current rises exponentially. Reverse bias: grows, only (nA) flows, independent of but doubling every 10 °C. Breakdown beyond PIV/PRV (Zener or avalanche). Junction capacitance falls as rises (varactor). Reverse recovery (ns to 1 µs).

Weeks 3–5 BJTs

Physics, modes, α and β

npn = n emitter (heavily doped) / p base (thin, lightly doped) / n collector. In active mode the forward EBJ injects electrons, about 1 % recombine in the thin base, the rest diffuse across and are swept into the collector by the reverse CBJ (diffusion dominates at the EBJ, drift at the CBJ). , , , . npn: , in, out; pnp all reversed. Traps

Weeks 1–2 (circuit tools, semiconductors, diodes)

  • Treating a negative rail as ground in a Thévenin (PT Q7: 6 V instead of 2 V). Every supply is a branch.
  • Divider used with a load on the middle node. It is only valid for series elements.
  • Units in : µm and mm not converted to cm. in J/K inside (needs eV/K), or in °C.
  • instead of . Doped material described as charged (it is neutral).
  • not recomputed for the stated temperature (20 °C is 25.27 mV).
  • dropped from , or used (PT Q2: 119 mV or 77.6 mV instead of 179 mV).
  • given when (slope, ) was asked, or the reverse.
  • No verification line after assuming diode states; OFF check written as instead of ; terms left out of the 3rd model; the shunt resistor at the input node ignored (PT Q3 pitfall: 0.333 mA).
  • Full-wave ripple without the 2 ( is not on the formula sheet). Bridge drops . Half-wave PIV doubles with a filter capacitor.
  • quoted as the dc output when a ripple is given (). Ripple factor 10 % is , not .
  • Zener sized at no load, or the no-load power check left out. A filtered supply uses the ripple valley as .
  • Clipper diode direction or battery sign misread (PT Q5: 16 V or −9 V instead of 0 / −1 V). Trace the only direction current can flow first.

Weeks 3–5 (BJTs)

  • WS4 handout mode table has saturation and cut-off swapped. Use the lecture table.
  • α = β/(1+α) or . Use α = β/(β+1), .
  • forgotten in the base loop (PT Q6: 71.5 µA instead of 35.3 µA). Load line drawn with only.
  • Approximate divider used without writing the test, or used when it fails (WS5 Q7: 16 % error). Never valid with .
  • Negative treated as a slip. It means saturation: redo with V and do not use .
  • Wrong β for a range: avoid saturation at , guarantee it at .
  • pnp with npn polarity (PT Q8: V). ; base and collector currents flow out.
  • and confused. Equal only with a grounded emitter.
  • β reading: “β at the Q-point” is from your graph readings, not the stated β quoted back.
  • AC built on a wrong Q-point. uses , uses . State (26 or 25 mV).
  • Bypassed and unbypassed mixed up. Partial bypass: DC uses the whole , AC only . Look for .
  • silently dropped when given and (slide 41: −368 becomes −324). Unbypassed stays even with .
  • Follower without , or when driven from (add ). Two-port loading used blindly on a follower or collector feedback.
  • CB given a minus sign, or ignored in front of a 30 Ω input.
  • Collector feedback taken as . It is and depends on the load.
  • Loaded gain larger than unloaded. That is a sign or reciprocal error.
  • Cascade: stage 1 not loaded by (with stage 2’s bias resistors); stage gains rounded before multiplying; not checked against the swing (Prac 4: 30 mV input would clip).
  • Darlington with one . Current mirror with in place of .

Weeks 6–8 (FETs)

  • Sign inside Shockley: , not 1.444. Only uses . A JFET with means a sign error. Only a D-MOS with of the enhancing sign can exceed .
  • Wrong or both roots kept. Test for each root and state which one you rejected and why.
  • or the JFET used for an E-MOSFET. Use and .
  • A voltage across . , so there is none. The battery polarity sets the sign of (WS8 Fig. 1–2).
  • when returns to . It is .
  • Skipping the saturation check. WS8 Q5 and WS9 Q4 give answers that fail it. Week 7 Example 2 sits on the edge.
  • Unbypassed treated as bypassed, or the reverse. Look for . The slide 53 entry is wrong. Use (exact form in the FET ac table).
  • Source follower . It is , dominated by . Drain feedback . It is .
  • Sign of the gain. CS is negative (slide 40 drops it: it should be −8.05). CG and the follower are positive. CE–CE is positive.
  • put in , or put in .
  • Unloaded stage gains multiplied in a cascade, or without the bias resistors. Do not round stage gains before multiplying.
  • Unit slips: µS against mS, in mA/V² used with in A, MΩ in .

Weeks 9–10 (differential amplifiers, op-amps, power amplifiers)

  • taken as the sum, or CMRR in dB put into the formula. Use the average and the ratio.
  • Non-inverting gain written as . It is .
  • rms, peak and p-p mixed in power formulas. Class A changes with , not with the signal.
